A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BrainMVP and contain readable methods, experiments, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Despite extensive reorganization, the same research work and corresponding evidence can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and classification experiments, label-efficiency studies, component ablations, and supplementary HD95 results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and reports additional visualizations of modality templates during pre-training.

M1.justification: The three proxy tasks and downstream template-consistency procedure are retained. However, Algorithm 1 changes the masked-pixel counter update from addition to an undefined circled-plus operator. The PDFs do not establish whether this is a notation error or an operative algorithm change.

E1.justification: The five pre-training sources and ten downstream tasks remain. v1's BrainAtlas row already cites IXI, so its relabeling adds no dataset. Although v2 Section 4.1 lists UCSF-PDGM as a downstream dataset, its tables and Appendix C.2 retain UPENN-GBM, supporting a naming inconsistency rather than changed coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark tables retain identical comparator rows, including MAE3D, SimMIM, MoCoV3, MG, TransVW, GVSL, Swin-UNETR*, VoCo, DAE, and M3AE. The label-efficiency and qualitative comparisons also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: The reported masking ratio changes from 0.8 to 0.875, contrastive learning begins at epoch 1000 instead of 900, and the BraTS-MET case count changes from 237 to 238. These are limited revisions to stated settings; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds a training-stage examination of template formation, showing initialization and epochs 200, 500, 1000, and 1500 instead of only trained templates. Component ablations, label-efficiency studies, and segmentation examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The reporting practice remains point estimates and curves without uncertainty bands.

E6.justification: All performance values in corresponding Dice, classification, ablation, and HD95 tables are identical. Label-efficiency plots and qualitative segmentation examples are also retained. The revised Figure 4 adds intermediate template snapshots, providing additional qualitative outcomes.

T1.justification: The reconstruction, symmetric contrastive, and downstream consistency objectives retain their mathematical substance. v2 reorganizes their presentation into per-example terms and explicit batch averaging. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: Both versions claim modality-aligned MRI pre-training through the same three proxy tasks, generalization across ten downstream benchmarks, and strong label efficiency using 40% of labeled data. The rewritten abstract and broader title do not establish a new substantive contribution claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds a template-maturation rationale for delaying contrastive learning and explicitly interprets segmentation examples as reducing under- and over-segmentation. Appendix D newly claims consistently smaller structural errors, although Table 6 includes counterexamples: MRBrainS13 HD95 is 4.72 for BrainMVP/UniFormer versus 2.95 for UniFormer from scratch.

D1.justification: v2 fills substantial reproducibility gaps by documenting downstream splits: generally 6:1:3, with five training and fifteen testing cases for MRBrainS13. It adds patient-level separation assurances, pre-training/test non-overlap, MRI-baseline reimplementation details, dataset-selection information, and a repository link. These are newly documented details, not established experimental redesigns.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned from natural-image vision-language learning and cross-domain SSL toward uni-modal versus mixed-modality medical SSL. v2 adds a dataset-distillation taxonomy with numerous additional references and explicitly relates its templates to performance matching, while removing the extended CLIP, Flamingo, BLIP-2, and ALBEF discussion.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten, and result discussions are compressed. Experiments and results are consolidated, while downstream formulation, preprocessing, and masking pseudocode move into an expanded, lettered supplement.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different conference-style layout, adds a conceptual Figure 1, replaces the static template display with a training-trajectory grid, and moves the unchanged downstream diagram into the supplement. The six label-efficiency panels are rearranged and reduced to a single-column display; tables and captions are extensively repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves important reporting omissions through explicit data splits, subject-separation assurances, baseline-training disclosures, and a repository pointer. Its reorganized explanation and template trajectories improve usability and transparency. These gains support a limited overall improvement, tempered by the undefined Algorithm 1 operator, inconsistent downstream dataset naming, and Appendix D's overbroad HD95 interpretation.
